independent_review.scope: dashboard bearer lifecycle, prepared exchange ownership, global admission accounting, tests, CMake target boundaries, and IOCP/application architecture
initial_findings: The bearer implementation originally held a mutex across injected secure-storage I/O, so shutdown could wait without a bound.
The bearer implementation originally did not revalidate cancellation, deadline, or shutdown after secure-storage retrieval.

The first prepared-exchange and admission tests exposed an atomic-wait terminal race, assertion teardown deadlock, moved-from SSE null dereference, HEAD shutdown ownership, repeated post-delivery actions, repeated close calls, ambiguous same-lease concurrency, frame error classification, partial thread-construction cleanup, and nested complete-exchange move ownership.
corrections: Bearer admission now uses an atomic flag, shutdown is nonblocking, in-flight lifetime is caller-owned and documented, and context is revalidated after retrieval with returned-secret wiping on rejection.

Prepared exchange now has an explicit empty moved-from state, null-safe subscription access, one-shot shutdown-action transfer and consumption, idempotent SSE close, and typed frame-size and integrity errors.
Admission tests use RAII worker-gate cleanup and cover partial thread-construction unwind; the admission lease is explicitly confined to one serialized connection state machine.
independent_review.post_correction_result: No remaining blocker found in the reviewed authentication, exchange, admission, test-lifetime, target-boundary, or ownership behavior.

behavior_proved: the dashboard bearer token uses the dashboard-specific manager.dashboard.bearer.v1 key, not the manager IPC nonce key, creates a 256-bit token through an injected generator, encodes exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, and stores or retrieves the token only through the injected secure-storage abstraction

the dashboard bearer token permits only one operation at a time without waiting, revalidates cancellation, deadline, and shutdown after injected storage calls, wipes rejected and moved-from secret buffers, and permits nonblocking idempotent shutdown while documenting caller ownership of in-flight lifetime
request authorization now validates the dashboard bearer contract's exact encoded size using constant-time comparison semantics

the move-only prepared exchange represents either one bounded complete response or one SSE bootstrap plus unique subscription, has an explicit empty moved-from state, and validates compact and full frames independently

complete exchanges distinguish GET from HEAD body ownership, prohibit HEAD from owning a shutdown action, transfer post-delivery shutdown exactly once across nested and outer moves, and consume that action exactly once

SSE exchanges emit the exact initial comment ': connected realtime\n\n', treat null or empty frames as integrity failures, accept the exact maximum frame size, reject oversized frames as payload-too-large, and close subscriptions idempotently when ownership ends

the admission controller enforces one atomic global 8-short, 32-SSE, 40-total budget across listener generations, returns move-only RAII leases, atomically converts short leases to SSE leases, retains a short lease on failed conversion, and releases capacity on every tested destruction and unwind path
the dedicated ForgeConductor.Dashboard.Windows target keeps Windows admission implementation downstream of the platform-neutral dashboard protocol target

ADR P16-006 fixes the remaining dashboard application and transport ownership boundary: application handler through IManagerClient, separate bounded handler executor, one process-owned IOCP with four socket workers, literal loopback and exclusive bind, bounded deadlines, two-phase rebind, one retiring generation, and shutdown only after response delivery
